candidate.name: Example Candidate
candidate.cv_summary: Physics graduate with experience in Python, statistical modelling, data visualisation, research and collaborative technical projects.

job_requirements: Interest in financial services and responsible AI

main_question.question: Why are you interested in joining Lloyds Banking Group as a Data Science and AI graduate?
main_question.reason: The role requires clear motivation for financial services, data science and the organisation.

responses.question: Why are you interested in joining Lloyds Banking Group as a Data Science and AI graduate?
responses.answer: I want to apply my analytical background to problems that affect a large number of customers. Lloyds appeals to me because it is investing heavily in data and technology, and the graduate scheme would let me develop through different placements.

strengths: Directly explains interest in the role
Connects data science with customer impact
Shows awareness of the rotational graduate structure
improvements: Include a more specific reason for choosing Lloyds
Link previous experience more clearly to the role
evaluation.suggested_follow_up_focus: Ask for a specific Lloyds initiative and a relevant example from the candidate's background.

responses.question: Which aspect of Lloyds' work in data or technology is most relevant to your interests?
responses.answer: I am particularly interested in how data can improve operational resilience and customer service. In my degree, I used Python to analyse complex datasets and explain the results clearly, so I would like to apply those skills in a commercial setting.

strengths: Links personal technical experience to the role
Identifies a commercially relevant area
Provides a clearer explanation of transferable skills
improvements: Name a specific Lloyds programme, platform or priority
Explain the expected business impact in more detail

strengths: Clear motivation for using data in a customer-focused organisation
Good connection between academic experience and the graduate role
improvements: Explain why Lloyds is preferable to other employers

main_question.question: Tell me about a time you worked with others to solve a difficult problem.
main_question.reason: The job description emphasises collaboration across technical and non-technical teams.

responses.question: Tell me about a time you worked with others to solve a difficult problem.
responses.answer: During a university group project, our team had to analyse a large dataset and present the results. We divided the work, met regularly and completed the project successfully.

strengths: Provides a relevant teamwork example
Mentions organisation and regular communication
improvements: Describe the difficulty in more detail
Include a clear and measurable outcome
evaluation.suggested_follow_up_focus: Ask what the candidate personally did and what obstacle the team encountered.

responses.question: What was your individual responsibility within the team?
responses.answer: I was responsible for cleaning the dataset and writing the Python code used to produce the main visualisations. I also explained the analysis to the rest of the group so that we could agree on the conclusions.

strengths: Clearly states individual ownership
Demonstrates technical and communication skills
Shows contribution to shared decision making
improvements: Add evidence of the scale or complexity of the dataset
Explain how the work changed the final outcome
evaluation.suggested_follow_up_focus: Ask for the final result and how success was measured.

responses.question: What was the final outcome, and how did you know the team had been successful?
responses.answer: We delivered the project before the deadline and received a first-class mark. The cleaned dataset also reduced errors in our analysis, and the visualisations were highlighted as one of the strongest parts of the presentation.

strengths: Provides a measurable academic outcome
Explains the impact of the candidate's work
Completes the example with a clear result
improvements: Combine the full example into one concise STAR response

strengths: Strong technical contribution
Clear evidence of teamwork and communication
Good measurable outcome after follow-up questioning
improvements: Include the strongest details in the initial answer
Use the STAR structure without needing repeated prompting

main_question.question: Describe a time when your original approach did not work. What did you do next?
main_question.reason: The role requires adaptability, technical judgement and evidence-based problem solving.

responses.question: Describe a time when your original approach did not work. What did you do next?
responses.answer: In my research project, an early model produced unstable results. I checked the assumptions, reviewed the code and tested smaller cases. I found that the boundary conditions were causing the instability, corrected them and then validated the revised output against expected behaviour.

strengths: Explains a genuine technical setback
Shows a logical diagnostic process
Demonstrates validation rather than assuming the fix worked
improvements: Add a measurable result or final project outcome
Briefly explain what was learnt and reused later
evaluation.suggested_follow_up_focus: Ask what the candidate learnt and how the fix affected the project.

responses.question: What did you learn from that experience, and how did it change your later work?
responses.answer: I learnt to test assumptions and boundary conditions on small cases before scaling up. I used that approach for the rest of the project, which made debugging faster and helped me produce a stable final simulation.

strengths: Shows clear learning and behavioural change
Connects the lesson to improved future performance
Demonstrates a repeatable problem-solving method
improvements: Quantify the time saved if possible

strengths: Strong structured problem-solving process
Good evidence of reflection and learning
Highly relevant technical example
